name: CDFW Restoration Grant Programs

funder.name: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

summary: California state grants, through a continuous concept-proposal process, for restoration of wetlands, mountain meadows, rivers, streams and habitat, covering planning, implementation and acquisition projects.

eligibility.rule: Acquisitions use willing sellers and DGS-approved fair market value
Multiple-landowner projects have written permission from all landowners or a designee
Applicant is not an out-of-state public entity unless a nonprofit registered with the California Secretary of State
Project is not required for environmental mitigation or compliance
Project is not under enforcement action by a regulatory agency
On-the-ground work has site control through the grant and for 25 years after, unless CDFW agrees otherwise

documents: 65% or higher design plans for implementation projects
Basis of design report for implementation projects
Without access: draft agreement, MOU or permission form. Multiple owners: written permission from all or their designee
Acquisition: executed purchase and sale or option agreement, or a willing-seller letter from each owner
Water rights and geomorphic factors questionnaire and applicable water-rights evidence for streamflow projects
Project budget using the CDFW template
Environmental compliance and permitting questionnaire for planning or implementation proposals
Land acquisition information attachment for acquisition proposals

applicant_types.quote: eligible applicants for funding include: Tribes, nonprofit organizations and public agencies.

access.quote: The application process begins with a concept proposal submitted through CDFW's WebGrants(opens in new tab) portal.

geography.quote: to accelerate the pace and scale of restoration throughout the state

co_finance_required.quote: Cost share is not required; however, proposals with higher proportions of secured cost share may receive higher scores during the evaluation process.

eligibility.quote: Acquisitions must be from willing sellers and at fair market value, as confirmed by an appraisal approved by the Department of General Services (DGS) Real Property Services Section.
For projects involving multiple landowners, all landowners or an appointed designee must provide written permission to complete the project.
public entities (except those that are nonprofit organizations registered with the California Secretary of State) are ineligible for funding
Grant funds cannot be used for projects required to meet environmental mitigation or compliance measures.
any project that is under an enforcement action by a regulatory agency will not be considered for funding.

Applications for implementation projects conducting on-the-ground work and requiring access to public or private property must submit documentation showing that they have adequate tenure to, and site control of, the properties to be restored for the term of the grant agreement and for at least 25 years after completion of the project (or an alternative term negotiated with CDFW)

after_award.quote: Grantees shall submit progress reports as outlined in the executed grant agreement to the CDFW grant manager for the duration of the grant.

documents.quote: Applicants should demonstrate land tenure, CEQA compliance, and submit 65% or higher design plans, a basis of design report, and technical studies.

When an applicant does not have land tenure/site access at the time of proposal submission, the applicant must submit a proposed site access agreement template, memorandum of understanding, or landowner permission form with the proposal.

For projects involving multiple landowners, all landowners or an appointed designee must provide written permission to complete the project. Acquisition proposals must include a signed purchase option agreement or willing seller letter from each landowner indicating that they are a willing participant in the proposed real estate transaction.

For post-1914 water rights, the applicant must submit a copy of a water right permit or license on file with the SWRCB. Applicants who divert water based on a riparian or pre-1914 water right must submit written evidence of the right to divert water and the priority in the watershed of that diversion right with their proposal.

If a purchase and sale or option agreement has been executed, it must be submitted with the application. If a purchase and sale or option agreement has not been executed, a willing seller letter from each landowner must be submitted with the application.

CDFW technical reviewers will evaluate all eligible and complete applications.
